title: Prefill Slab Adapter to Reduce Dequant Propagation in INT8/FP8 Paths
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce per-token latency and CPU overhead caused by repeated dequantization and re-quantization across the prefill -> decode boundary on mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) model paths. Implement a lightweight slab adapter in the prefill scheduler that preserves quantized activations when safe and routes kernel selection to quant-friendly kernels, avoiding unnecessary dequant propagation into decode kernels.
background: We observed a 10-18% token latency regression on long-context streaming workloads when models take an INT8/FP8 route then cross into decode kernels that expect FP16 activations. Current runtime performs eager dequantization at the prefill/dispatch boundary, which incurs memory traffic and additional kernel conversions for each prefill. Recent kernel work (ENG-74219, ENG-61892) prepared quant-friendly kernels but runtime still forces a full dequant at the scheduler boundary, losing benefits.
proposal: Introduce a 'prefill slab adapter' layer in the scheduler that: 1) tracks quantization metadata (scale/zero point, precision) alongside KV slabs; 2) annotates prefill slabs as 'quant-preserved' when following safety rules (no incompatible ops, calibration present); 3) selects downstream decode kernels that can accept quantized slabs or schedules lightweight in-place requantization only when required. The adapter will include a small fast-path for INT8->INT8 decode and an FP8 passthrough where supported. Fallback to existing dequant flow when safety checks fail.
design_decisions: Keep quant metadata as compact header (64 bits) per KV slab to minimize memory overhead
Perform safety checks at schedule time: op compatibility table + per-model config flags
Prioritize in-place requant over full dequant->requant when conversion necessary to reduce memory traffic
Expose a runtime flag `enable_slab_adapter` gated behind internal rollout for canary testing
implementation_notes: Add SlabMetadata struct and serialization/deserialization hooks for offload to host memory (C++ runtime) - ensure structure is POD and aligned
Extend scheduler to carry SlabMetadata with prefill units and flow it to kernel selection API
Kernel registry: add capability flags `accepts_int8_slab`, `accepts_fp8_slab` and query them during dispatch
Implement small adapter module that performs fast safety table checks (bitmask-based) to avoid branches in hot path
test_plan: Unit tests for SlabMetadata encode/decode across CPU/GPU boundary
Microbenchmarks: prefill+first-decode token latency for INT8/FP8 routes with slab_adapter on/off (measure p50/p95)
Fuzz schedule tests: inject incompatible op flags and assert fallback to dequant path
Integration test: end-to-end streaming with long context (>8k) to validate memory and correctness
A/B canary on 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours with rollout metrics collection (latency, error rate, cost per token)
risks: Incorrect metadata propagation could cause silent numerical drift if a quant-preserved slab is consumed by an incompatible kernel
Extra metadata per slab increases memory pressure for very large KV caches if not compacted
Complexity in kernel compatibility table might introduce subtle dispatch bugs leading to increased error rates
Canary failures could be customer-facing for enterprise customers with strict accuracy requirements
acceptance_criteria: 0) Feature flag `enable_slab_adapter` exists and defaults to off
1) When enabled, at least 70% of prefill slabs in INT8/FP8 routes are preserved end-to-end (preserved_count metric)
2) p50 token latency for target workloads improves by >=6% compared to baseline for quant paths with adapter enabled
3) No regression in model output accuracy outside tolerated delta (per-model eval suite) — report per-model drift
4) Canary metrics show <=1% change in error-rate and no customer-impacting incidents during 48h
5) Unit and integration tests pass in CI with coverage for safety-check branches
